elements.label: Figure 2.2
elements.description: Grouped vertical bar chart. Y-axis: '# of households (in millions)', scale 0 to 8. X-axis categories: Central Highlands, Mekong Delta, Midlands & Northern Mountains, Northern & Coastal Central, Red River Delta, Southeast. Legend: Kinh (teal), Ethnic minority (orange). No values are printed on the bars. Approximate readings: Central Highlands Kinh ~1.1, ethnic minority ~0.4; Mekong Delta Kinh ~4.3, ethnic minority ~0.3; Midlands & Northern Mountains Kinh ~1.6, ethnic minority ~1.7; Northern & Coastal Central Kinh ~5.0, ethnic minority ~0.5; Red River Delta Kinh ~6.5, ethnic minority ~0.1; Southeast Kinh ~5.0, ethnic minority ~0.25. Kinh households are far more numerous in every region except the Midlands & Northern Mountains, where ethnic minority households are about equal to or slightly above Kinh households. Source: World Bank staff calculations using the VHLSS, 2020.

elements.label: Figure 2.3
elements.description: Grouped vertical bar chart. Y-axis: '# of households (in millions)', scale 0 to 8. X-axis categories: No education, Primary, Lower Secondary, Upper Secondary, Vocational, Tertiary. Legend: 2010 (teal), 2020 (orange). Values printed on bars (2010 / 2020): No education 1.5 / 1.4; Primary 4.0 / 3.5; Lower Secondary 5.7 / 6.9; Upper Secondary 4.1 / 5.5; Vocational 3.7 / 4.7; Tertiary 3.0 / 4.7. Note: Maximum level of completed education of any household member. Source: World Bank staff calculations using the VHLSS, 2010 and 2020. The pattern shows the number of households with lower-level maximum education falling and higher-level maximum education rising between 2010 and 2020, with Tertiary rising from 3.0 to 4.7 million.

elements.label: Figure 2.4
elements.description: Grouped vertical bar chart. Y-axis: '# of households (in millions)', scale 0 to 15. X-axis categories: Agriculture, Manufacturing, Services. Legend: 2010 (teal), 2020 (orange). Values printed on bars (2010 / 2020): Agriculture 11.6 / 9.5; Manufacturing 8.3 / 12.2; Services 9.6 / 13.1. Note: Not exclusive; households with multiple working adults can be engaged in multiple sectors as main jobs. Source: World Bank staff calculations using the VHLSS, 2010 and 2020. Agriculture declined while manufacturing and services increased, with agriculture moving from the largest to the smallest of the three sectors.
